question: A 4-month-old boy is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. He was born at 36 weeks' gestation. The mother has had no prenatal care. His 6-year-old sister has a history of osteosarcoma. He is exclusively breast fed. He is at the 60th percentile for height and weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows inward deviation of the right eye. Indirect ophthalmoscopy shows a white reflex in the right eye and a red reflex in the left eye. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Inward deviation of the right eye" -> "White reflex in the right eye" -> "Red reflex in the left eye" -> "Suspicion of retinoblastoma" -> "Fundus examination" -> 80% CHAIN: "Exclusively breastfed" -> "Risk of galactosemia due to galactose exposure" -> "Screen for galactosemia" -> 70% CHAIN: "Family history of osteosarcoma" -> "Concern for genetic predisposition to cancer" -> "Evaluate for genetic syndromes associated with retinoblastoma" -> "Fundus examination" -> 75% CHAIN: "No prenatal care" -> "Risk of congenital infections" -> "Serum rubella titers" -> 80%
enhanced_information: Given the suspicion of retinoblastoma based on the clinical findings of inward deviation of the right eye and white reflex in the right eye, the most appropriate next step in management is a fundus examination. This is supported by the concern for genetic predisposition to cancer due to the family history of osteosarcoma, which warrants evaluation for genetic syndromes associated with retinoblastoma. Screening for galactosemia or performing visual training exercises are not indicated based on the current presentation. Additionally, considering the risk of congenital infections due to the lack of prenatal care, obtaining serum rubella titers is not the immediate next step in management.
analysis: Given the clinical suspicion of retinoblastoma in a 4-month-old boy with inward deviation of the right eye and a white reflex in that eye, the most appropriate next step is a fundus examination. This is crucial to confirm the diagnosis and initiate timely management. Screening for galactosemia, visual training exercises, and serum rubella titers are not indicated in this context. The family history of osteosarcoma raises concern for genetic predisposition to cancer, emphasizing the need for evaluation for genetic syndromes associated with retinoblastoma.
